summary.text: 回 is associated with turning and circular motion, and commonly means “return” or counts an occurrence. Its earliest referent and the relationship between these uses remain uncertain.

formation.text: 回 is treated in one account as a pictograph of a revolving loop; another describes its inner shape as resembling rotation within 囗. A competing analysis proposes that 囘 “whirl” and 回 “around” were originally distinct graphs and words. The depicted object and the relationship between these analyses remain unresolved.

components.text: 回 is treated as a whole picture associated with circular motion. Shuowen describes an outer 囗 and an inner revolving shape, but this does not establish them as independent components.

history.text: Shang–Zhou forms are described as revolving loops; Warring States Qin forms as two enclosed rings; and later forms as following those rings. This reported sequence is not a verified series of dated artifacts.

Shuowen describes an outer 囗 enclosing a shape resembling rotation. A competing proposal treats 囘 and 回 as originally distinct graphs and words, with 回 made for “around” and modeled on 圍; their relationship remains unresolved.

In 迴, 回 is reported as a sound-and-meaning component. The two graphs share Mandarin huí and have corresponding historical readings in the cited reconstruction systems; this compound role does not establish a phonetic part in 回’s own origin.

uncertainties.text: The spiral or circular-motion interpretation is supported, but the depicted object and exact earliest meaning remain uncertain. The competing distinction between 囘 and 回 cannot be fully assessed from the available account.

The earliest attested sense and any chronology linking turning, returning, replying, and occurrence-counting have not been established. Dictionary glosses and literary examples do not by themselves show that sequence.
The proposed derivation of the ethnonym 回回 from Uyghur or Old Turkic forms remains unverified; the source word and historical sound match are uncertain.
The sound relationship between 回 and 迴 is supported, but when 迴 arose or when the graphs became variant or distributionally distinct spellings is unresolved.

senses.text: ‘Return’ is a common current meaning. Its historical relationship to turning or revolving remains unresolved.
回 can refer to one time or occurrence and serve as a counter. The evidence does not date this use or show how it developed.

limitations.text: The sources propose turning or revolving as an original meaning, but this proposed meaning is not independently established as an attested use. The available examples and glosses do not establish the chronology or semantic pathway connecting it with returning and occurrence-counting.

The proposed 回回 ethnonym borrowing is a separate account of a word written with this graph, not evidence of a semantic development from 回. The proposed source and sound-based borrowing remain unverified.

overview.text: 回 is associated with turning or circular motion and commonly means “return”; it can also count an occurrence. Its earliest referent and the development of these uses remain uncertain.

components.text: Read 回 as one whole picture associated with circular motion; its outer and inner shapes are not established as separate meaning-bearing parts.
